speaker: Doctor
text: GREETING: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the nature of these symptoms, can you tell me if your double vision is constant or if it goes away when you close one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with symptoms triggered by looking up or down, suggests a neuromuscular issue. Given your difficulty climbing stairs and upper limb weakness, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty speaking or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.
